change_summary: The notice is titled as a retraction of this paper, 'Detecting phishing websites using machine learning technique'. PLOS ONE retracted the article because of concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process. The concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. The author did not respond directly or could not be reached.
evaluation: Your Section 3 cites Dutta [14] as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM, and says you chose it on the strength of the reported results. That paper reports 97.4% and 96.8% accuracy for LURL. Your Section 4 starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14]. The paper reports those settings as hidden size 650, learning rate 1.0 and decay 0.73. The retraction is over concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process. The notice says these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, which touches both your detector choice and your starting settings. The impact is high, because the paper is your main evidence for the design and your parameter source.
recommendation: Your Section 3 cites Dutta [14] as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM detector, and your Section 4 starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14]. PLOS ONE retracted the article because of concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process, and the concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor before going further, since editing the text will not fix a design that rests on this paper. Replace or independently support the evidence for the detector choice, re-derive your starting settings from a reliable source, and cite the retraction notice in the reference entry.
